status: [V] FAIL: symbolized SIGSEGV inside FIDESlib's own multi-GPU ContextData/SetupConstants construction path
task: First real test of FIDESlib multi-GPU device sharding as a lever for the two-block gate (fhe_fides_gpu_multiblock_blocks0_1_refresh_FAIL_20260724 and its single-GPU OOM/heap-corruption diagnoses in the depth50/depth58 bisection runs). CLI, launcher, and scheduler were extended to accept a comma-separated GPU list (--gpu N[,N...], SetDevices({N,...})) and reserve/launch on 2 physical GPUs atomically; this run exercises that path for the first time on real hardware.

config.note: Committed source unchanged from the pinned single-GPU configuration; only --gpu was given a 2-element device list. No depth/digit/slot tuning in this run.

observed.setup_progress: GenCryptoContext, Enable(...), EvalBootstrapSetup, KeyGen, EvalMultKeyGen, EvalRotateKeyGen (63 keys), EvalBootstrapKeyGen all completed; both GPU 0 and GPU 1 device banners printed (both physical devices enumerated correctly) before the crash
observed.failure_message: SIGSEGV, exit code 139 (via nohup wrapper); peak VRAM only ~8.7 GiB per GPU at time of crash, ruling out OOM
observed.diagnostic_method: cuda-gdb --batch -ex run -ex 'thread apply all bt', invoked directly against the rebuilt multi-GPU binary inside the pinned dnagpt-fideslib:786c-asymfix2 container with --gpus '"device=5,6"'. Plain gdb/strace were previously reported non-viable on this binary (SIGSEGV storm under ptrace, per fhe_fides_gpu_multiblock_bisect_depth58_backtrace_FAIL_20260724's task note); cuda-gdb worked cleanly and produced one clean SIGSEGV with a stable, reproducible backtrace on the main thread among ~291 total threads (OpenMP worker pool).

verdict: [V] The crash is not GPU memory exhaustion (only ~8.7 GiB/GPU in use, far below 80GB) and is not the same code path as the single-GPU depth50/depth58 OOM/heap-corruption diagnoses (AddBootstrapPlaintexts -> ... -> GPUmalloc). It is a distinct, earlier failure inside FIDESlib::SetupConstants, called from the multi-device ContextData constructor with a 2-element devices vector, during a cudaMemcpyHostToDevice. This is consistent with the prior risk assessment that FIDESlib's own examples and test suite only ever exercise devices={0} and never a real multi-GPU device list -- this is a genuine, previously-unexercised bug or unmet precondition in FIDESlib's multi-GPU device-context setup itself, not a configuration or memory-sizing problem on the DNAGPT side. `[U]` Root-causing the exact faulting cudaMemcpy call requires either a debug (non-Release) FIDESlib build for line-level symbols, or a `compute-sanitizer`/`cuda-memcheck` pass, neither attempted yet. Multi-GPU sharding is not a usable lever for the two-block gate until this is fixed upstream or worked around (e.g. explicit per-device stream/context serialization around SetupConstants); reverting to reducing batch_slots/rotation-key count remains the more tractable single-GPU-only path.

provenance.docker_gpus_flag_note: Docker 29.3.1 / nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.1 rejects a bare '--gpus device=5,6' with 'cannot set both Count and DeviceIDs on device request'; requires nested-quoted '--gpus "\"device=5,6\""' so Docker's own CSV parser treats the comma-separated list as one value. launch_brev_multiblock.sh was fixed accordingly before this run.
